media_strategy.selection_principle: LEAN budget: data-driven charts and CSS/SVG/interactive are the backbone; exactly one generated hero image; no video, no music. Audio is a synced Web Audio sonification (no generated file).

chart.reason: A behavioral survey of 19 phrases x 5,174 people is fundamentally quantitative — distribution/spread, ranking, and rank-comparison charts carry the whole argument.

image.reason: One generated hero image sets an editorial, conceptual tone (the word 'likely' fragmenting into many numbers) without forcing decorative imagery elsewhere. LEAN budget = exactly one image.

video.reason: LEAN budget forbids video, and there is no event/process/transformation in this abstract behavioral dataset that motion would clarify. The 'fragmentation' idea is delivered by the static hero instead.

audio.reason: The last-digit distribution is extraordinarily spiky (53.6% on 0, 31.2% on 5, 0.5% on 4). A click-to-play Web Audio sonification mapping each digit's frequency to pitch/volume lets the reader HEAR the round-number bias as two loud spikes — synced to the bar chart. No generated audio file (LEAN); pure oscillator.

interactive_or_map.reason: No geography worth mapping, but two surprising findings are best felt before being told: a guess-first reveal for 'realistic possibility' (the spine), and an explorable rank-flip for likely-vs-probable.

des_teaser.label: Guess-first teaser: put a number on 'realistic possibility'

content.initial_state: Full-viewport dark screen. Centered prompt: 'Someone says an outcome is a “realistic possibility.” What probability do they mean?' A large 0–100% slider sits below, starting at 50, with a live readout of the reader's value.
content.trigger: Reader drags the slider and clicks 'Lock it in'.
content.transition: The reader's marker drops onto a horizontal 0–100 strip; then the crowd's full distribution of 'realistic possibility' estimates fades in behind it as a translucent histogram, with the UK official 40–50% band highlighted.
content.payoff: Reader sees where their private guess falls among 5,174 others and how far it is from the official 40–50% band — the whole thesis in one move. Their guess is stored (sessionStorage) and recalled in the closing section.

des_teaser.brief: The first thing the reader sees, before the headline. A single slider + 'Lock it in' button over a dark full-bleed screen. After locking, reveal the crowd histogram (ana_03 10-pt bins) with the 40–50 band tinted. Store the value for edt_08. This makes the reader a participant in the experiment, not a spectator.
des_teaser.rationale: An interactive teaser beats a passive hero because the core finding (you and the crowd disagree about a single word) can be FELT in one drag. Chosen over video/image teaser per the interactive-preference rule and LEAN budget.

des_hero.label: Conceptual hero image — 'likely' fragmenting into numbers

content.prompt: A cinematic editorial conceptual still: the single word 'LIKELY' in elegant serif type dissolving into a spreading cloud of faint translucent percentage numbers drifting apart against a deep charcoal background, soft warm rim light, shallow depth of field, minimalist, no chart, restrained, high-end magazine aesthetic

des_hero.brief: Single generated image placed under the headline after the teaser. The word 'likely' breaking into a scatter of numbers visually states the thesis. Full-width within story column, dark, atmospheric.
des_hero.rationale: The one image allowed by the LEAN budget; conceptual rather than decorative, it earns its slot by literally depicting the core claim.

des_01.label: Realistic Possibility distribution vs official band

content.interaction: hover tooltip with count per 10-pt bin

style.palette: muted with one accent for the 40-50 official band

des_01.brief: Histogram of how 5,174 people rated 'realistic possibility' in 10-point bins. The single 40–50 bar (the UK official band) is tinted in the accent colour; everything else muted grey. Annotate that only 17.5% fell inside the official band and 64% read it as better than even. This is also the chart revealed by the teaser.
des_01.rationale: A histogram makes the smear across 0–100 and the tiny official-band slice immediately visible — the chart equivalent of the hook.

des_02.label: The 19-phrase ladder (mean + spread)

content.interaction: hover tooltip showing mean, median, q25–q75, std

des_02.brief: Horizontal dot-and-range chart: 19 phrases on the y-axis sorted by mean (Almost No Chance at bottom, Will Happen at top). Each row shows a dot at the mean and a thin bar from q25 to q75. Already hints that some rows (Realistic Possibility, the modal verbs) have wide bars while extremes are pinpoints — setting up edt_03. Tooltip reveals full stats.
des_02.rationale: Echoes Kucharski's own ranked dot-plot but adds the IQR range so the reassuring ladder visibly carries its own contradiction.

des_03.label: Disagreement ranking (spread of estimates)

content.interaction: hover tooltip with std, IQR, mean

des_03.brief: Horizontal bar chart of all 19 phrases ranked by standard deviation (disagreement). Realistic Possibility's bar is longest and accent-highlighted; About Even/Almost Certain shortest. This is the centrepiece chart — the inverse of the tidy ladder.
des_03.rationale: Directly visualizes the lead finding: consensus collapses in the middle and at hedge words. The reversal from edt_02's order is the 'aha'.

des_04.label: Likely-vs-Probable rank-flip explorer

content.initial_state: Two columns of the 19 phrases ranked 1–19. A toggle: 'Rank by: [Average value] / [Head-to-head win rate]'. Connector lines link each phrase between its two ranks.
content.transition: Ranks animate; phrases that swap places (Likely/Probable, Improbable/Little Chance, Might/Could Happen) have their connector lines highlighted in the accent colour and slide visibly.
content.payoff: Reader sees that almost everything stays put (Spearman 0.989) EXCEPT the near-tie words — and that 'Likely' and 'Probable' literally trade places depending on how you measure.

des_04.brief: A slope/bump-style interactive built from ana_11 (abs_rank vs pw_rank). Two ranked lists with connector lines; toggling the ranking method animates positions and highlights the 1–2 rank flips. Callout box pins the title-fight numbers: Likely avg 72.6 / win-rate 68.5%; Probable avg 71.4 / win-rate 77.7%.
des_04.rationale: The flip is the cleverest finding and is best understood by doing the swap yourself rather than reading two rankings side by side.

des_05.label: Closest contests bar (winner share near 50%)

content.interaction: hover tooltip with n and winner share

style.palette: muted, accent on Likely vs Probable

des_05.brief: Horizontal bars for the closest head-to-head contests; x-axis starts at 50% (a baseline reference line at 50 = perfect disagreement). Shorter bar = closer to a coin flip. Likely vs Probable accent-highlighted. Note: x scale must NOT start at zero — domain 50–65.
des_05.rationale: Quantifies how genuinely close the title fight and its neighbours are; pairs with the rank-flip explorer.

des_06.label: Self-consistency stat callout (96.6%)

content.label: of people gave the same answer when secretly shown the same pair twice — the disagreement is between us, not within us

des_06.brief: Big 72px stat 96.6% with the explanatory label below. Anchors the pivotal 'between people, not within them' claim.
des_06.rationale: One number that reframes the whole piece; deserves headline treatment rather than a chart.

des_07.label: Last-digit spike chart

style.palette: muted with accent on digits 0 and 5

des_07.brief: Bar chart of the share of all 98,306 estimates ending in each digit 0–9. Two towering accent bars at 0 (53.6%) and 5 (31.2%); the rest tiny, with 4 nearly invisible (0.5%). The visual shape IS the finding.
des_07.rationale: A last-digit histogram is the canonical way to expose round-number bias and reads instantly.

des_08.label: Sonification of the last-digit spikes

content.why_audio: Hearing the distribution makes the round-number bias visceral: two loud, high spikes on 0 and 5 and near-silence elsewhere — the same shape as the bar chart, but felt.
content.trigger: Click 'Play the digits' button beneath the last-digit chart (never autoplay).
content.ui_form: chart-synced sonification — each of the 10 bars lights up in turn (0→9) while a tone plays; pitch rises with the digit, and LOUDNESS maps to that digit's share, so 0 and 5 ring out and 4 is a whisper.
content.fallback: If Web Audio is unavailable or muted, the bar chart fully communicates the pattern; the button shows a tooltip. Pure oscillator — no audio file (LEAN budget).
content.novelty_note: Not a generic tone card: the sequence is bound to the chart bars and only meaningful while watching them light up; loudness (not just pitch) carries the data.

des_08.brief: Web Audio API click-to-play sonification reading the 10 last-digit shares left to right; gain scaled to each share so digits 0 and 5 are loud and 1–4,6–9 are faint. Sync each note to a highlight pulse on the matching bar in des_07. Small legend: 'pitch = digit, loudness = how often people used it'.
des_08.rationale: LEAN-compatible audio (no generated file) that genuinely adds meaning — the spikiness is more memorable heard than seen.

des_09.label: Optimism by country (small-effect chart)

content.interaction: hover tooltip with optimism (pp) and sample size n

style.annotation: Note the x-axis spans only -3 to +3 points — these differences are small.

des_09.brief: Diverging horizontal bar chart of country optimism (term-centered pp), sorted descending; US accent-highlighted at top, Norway most negative at bottom. CRITICAL: x-axis fixed to -3..+3 with an explicit annotation that the whole spread is under 3 points, so the chart cannot exaggerate the effect. Tooltip shows n so small-sample countries are caveated.
des_09.rationale: Honest visualization of a real-but-tiny effect; the constrained axis and annotation enforce the editor's 'effects are small' mandate.

des_10.label: Age optimism mini-chart (color/secondary)

content.interaction: hover tooltip with optimism and n (flag small n for Under 18 / 75+)

des_10.brief: Small vertical bar chart of optimism by age band in age order. Tooltip surfaces sample sizes so the Under-18 (+3.11, n=19) and 75+ (n=79) bars are visibly caveated as thin samples. Secondary to des_09.
des_10.rationale: Reinforces that age is among the weakest signals; kept compact to avoid a chart streak and to subordinate it to the country chart.

page_rhythm.text_visual_pattern: interactive-first (teaser) → prose → chart, alternating so no three charts run in a row; the rank-flip explorer and the sonification break up the chart cadence
page_rhythm.anti_sameness_notes: Lead with a guess-first slider rather than a hero image or chart; reuse the reader's own stored guess at the close; use loudness-mapped sonification instead of the usual tone card; constrain demographic axes to prevent exaggeration. Only one generated image, used conceptually.
page_rhythm.typography_notes: Large serif headline; 72px stat callout for 96.6%; pull-quote treatment for the Kent 20–80% anecdote; section dividers as thin hairlines; phrase names in a monospace-ish accent to feel like 'terms'.
